title: RabbitMQ Fundamentals
description: Learn the core concepts of RabbitMQ including exchanges, queues, bindings, and the AMQP protocol.

data.text: RabbitMQ is one of the most widely deployed open-source message brokers. It implements the Advanced Message Queuing Protocol (AMQP) and provides a robust platform for routing messages between applications. Understanding its core abstractions — producers, exchanges, queues, and consumers — is essential for building decoupled systems.

A RabbitMQ producer publishes messages to an exchange rather than directly to a queue. The exchange then routes messages to one or more queues based on rules called bindings. Consumers read messages from queues. This decoupling allows producers and consumers to evolve independently.

terms.definition: A routing component that receives messages from producers and pushes them to queues based on exchange type and routing keys.
A buffer that stores messages until a consumer is ready to process them.
A rule that connects an exchange to a queue, specifying how messages should be routed.
A string used by the exchange to decide which queues receive a given message.

data.title: Four Built-in Exchange Types
items: Direct: Routes to queues whose binding key exactly matches the message's routing key.
Fanout: Ignores routing key and broadcasts to all bound queues.
Topic: Routes using pattern matching (e.g., 'user.*' or 'order.#').
Headers: Routes based on message header attributes rather than routing key.

data.title: Choose the Right Exchange
data.text: Use a direct exchange for task distribution among workers, a fanout exchange for broadcast notifications, and a topic exchange for event routing based on categories like 'order.created' or 'payment.failed'.

data.title: Key Benefits
items: Flexible routing via exchange types and bindings
Supports both point-to-point and publish-subscribe patterns
Message acknowledgment and requeue for reliability
Rich management and monitoring via HTTP API and Prometheus plugin

data.title: Clustering and High Availability
data.text: RabbitMQ clustering replicates queues across nodes, but mirrored queues are deprecated in favor of quorum queues. Use quorum queues for durable, replicated messaging with automatic failover.

items.question: What is the difference between a direct and topic exchange?
items.answer: A direct exchange routes by exact routing key match, while a topic exchange supports wildcard patterns like '#' (match one or more words) and '*' (match exactly one word).

items.question: Do messages persist across RabbitMQ restarts?
items.answer: Only if you declare queues as durable, publish messages with deliveryMode = 2 (persistent), and use quorum queues. Otherwise messages are lost on restart.

items.question: Can multiple consumers read from the same queue?
items.answer: Yes. RabbitMQ dispatches messages in round-robin fashion among active consumers on the same queue. This is the competitive consumer pattern.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Producers send to exchanges, not directly to queues
Exchanges use exchange types to route messages to queues
Bindings connect queues to exchanges with routing rules
Quorum queues provide durability and replication
data.takeaway: RabbitMQ's exchange-queue-bindings model gives you flexible, decoupled message routing.
